program_name: Economics (Two-Year Master Degree in Economics / Master Program in Economics)
teaching_language: Fully English-taught. This is a stand-alone Italian second-cycle degree (laurea magistrale) of the Department of Economics, Social Studies, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ESOMAS), delivered entirely in English. It is NOT an English pathway inside an Italian-named degree, and it is NOT an interuniversity/joint degree: the Apply@UniTo course record and the UNITO key-information sheet both state 'Study language: English', and the programme site states that all courses of the Two-Year Master Degree in Economics are taught in English. Note: the programme does run optional double-degree agreements with partner universities (e.g. Universite de Rennes 1, Universidade do Minho/Braga) and has links with Collegio Carlo Alberto (Allievi honours track/scholarships), but the base degree awarded is a single UNITO LM-56 degree.
campus: Turin (Torino), Italy - Department of Economics, Social Studies, Applied Mathematics and Statistics (ESOMAS), within the School of Management and Economics (SME). Department reception: (+39) 011 670 6191.
degree_class: LM-56 (Scienze dell'economia / Economics). UNITO internal course code: 2304M23. Apply@UniTo course id: 282. 120 ECTS, nominal duration 2 years.
admission_type: Open access - 'course without restricted number of places' (no numerus clausus, no entrance exam and no ranking-based selection). Admission is instead by verification of prerequisites: the admission committee checks the curricular credits, the undergraduate grade/GPA and the English level. If one or more admission requirements are not met, the applicant may be called for an interview at the discretion of the admission committee. Applications are evaluated on a rolling basis. A separate territorial cap does exist for one applicant category only: the Apply@UniTo course record states the programme has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad.
application_deadline_eu: A.y. 2026/2027. (a) Applicants holding a FOREIGN qualification (Italians, EU citizens and equivalents, and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy) apply on Apply@UniTo and may use either the 1st admission call, 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026 (open to all applicants for postgraduate degree programmes), or the 4th admission call for open-access postgraduate degree programmes only, 25 August - 8 September 2026, which is expressly reserved to Italians, EU and EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy. The live Apply@UniTo page for course 282 currently shows the application deadline '8 Sept 2026, 23:59:59 Central European Time' with the note that this call is reserved to European applicants and non-EU applicants legally residing in Italy. (b) 'Domestic' applicants holding an ITALIAN university degree (typically a Laurea Triennale) do NOT use Apply@UniTo; they apply through the programme's own online form, open from 1 March to 20 August. [uncertain: the 1 March - 20 August domestic window is taken from the programme's 'How to apply' page, whose last recorded update is 25/03/2024; the exact 2026 dates should be re-checked.]
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU citizens residing abroad who require an entry visa must apply on Apply@UniTo within the 1st admission call only: 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026. The later calls in the 2026/2027 calendar (3rd: 1 July - 14 September 2026 for restricted-number programmes; 4th: 25 August - 8 September 2026 for open-access postgraduate programmes; 5th: 25 August - 19 October 2026) are all expressly reserved to Italians, EU and EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy, so they are not available to visa applicants. Visa applicants must in addition submit the pre-enrolment application on the Universitaly platform by 15 July 2026 (one degree programme only on Universitaly). Only 50 places are available for non-European applicants residing abroad. [uncertain: the 15 July 2026 Universitaly date was read from a search-engine rendering of en.unito.it, which is Cloudflare-blocked to direct fetch.]
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance examination and no admission test (the programme is open access). The only possible selection step is an INTERVIEW, held at the discretion of the admission committee when one or more admission requirements are not met: (a) if the English certification is missing, the interview is conducted in English and the candidate must be able to write, speak and read fluently; (b) if the other (curricular/GPA) requirements are missing, the interview covers fundamentals of Microeconomics, Macroeconomics, Mathematics and Statistics. The interview verifies the adequacy of the applicant's background and focuses on the topics whose low marks pulled the undergraduate GPA below 90% of the maximum; it may include a written part. Recommended preparation textbooks published by the programme: Pindyck & Rubinfeld 'Microeconomics' (ch. 1-12, 14-18); A. Chiang 'Fundamental Methods of Mathematical Economics'; Wonnacott & Wonnacott 'Introductory Statistics'; Sheldon M. Ross 'Introduction to Probability Models'; Blanchard 'Macroeconomics' (all chapters except section three). International (Apply@UniTo) applicants may also be invited to an online interview; applications are evaluated on a rolling basis. Separately, two optional intensive crash courses in Mathematics and Probability run in the first two weeks of September before teaching starts (preparatory, not selective).
academic_requirements: 1) A first-cycle degree (Bachelor's) earned after at least 3 years of university education is required. Applicants are NOT required to already hold the Bachelor's degree when filing the application, but must be able to obtain it preferably before courses begin and in any case no later than the final enrolment deadline (around mid-December). 2) QUANTITATIVE/ECONOMIC BACKGROUND: at least one tenth of total undergraduate credits in Economics (i.e. 18 credits in courses classified SECS-P/01 to SECS-P/06 for an Italian degree) AND at least one tenth of total undergraduate credits in Mathematics and Statistics (i.e. 18 credits in SECS-S/01 to SECS-S/06 or MAT/06 for an Italian degree). Italian bachelor's degrees in classes L-18 (ex L-17) and L-33 (ex L-28) are deemed to satisfy these two credit requirements by default. 3) GRADE THRESHOLD: Grade Point Average or undergraduate final grade equal to or above 90% of the highest possible grade (99/110 for an Italian degree). The Apply@UniTo entry-qualification text phrases the merit test as satisfying AT LEAST ONE of: (i) a first-cycle degree issued by an institution in the top 12.5% of the RePEc ranking of Economics departments, or (ii) a final grade greater than or equal to 9/10 of the highest possible grade (e.g. 99/110 for an Italian degree). 4) Applicants are expected to have an appropriate background in the topics covered by the recommended textbooks. 5) If one or more requirements are not met, the candidate may be invited to an interview at the committee's discretion rather than being automatically rejected. 6) PLACES: no general numerus clausus ('course without restricted number of places'); the only cap is 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad. [uncertain: the relationship between the microsite wording (credits AND GPA all required) and the Apply@UniTo wording (RePEc-ranking OR grade >= 9/10) is not fully reconciled in the official texts; the microsite admission page's last recorded update is 25/03/2021.]
language_requirements: ENGLISH - CEFR B2 minimum, evidenced by an international certificate. Apply@UniTo (course 282) states applicants must hold an international certification attesting at least a CEFR B2 level, and that the certification must be no more than three years old. Accepted certificates and minimum scores: Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE); Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE); Cambridge First Certificate of English (FCE) with minimum score 173 (grade B); PTE Academic minimum 65; IELTS minimum 5.5 out of 9 with no component below 5.5; TOEFL iBT minimum 69 out of 120 with no component below 17; Trinity College ISE II. WAIVER/ALTERNATIVE: instead of a certificate, applicants may upload an official document issued by their previous university stating that the medium of instruction was English. FURTHER FALLBACK: the programme's own admission page states that if the English certification is missing the candidate may be considered for an interview conducted in English, in which the candidate must be able to write, speak and read fluently. ITALIAN - no Italian language requirement for this English-taught programme (the B2 Italian certificate rule that UNITO applies to non-EU visa applicants concerns free-admission postgraduate programmes taught in Italian, not this one).
required_documents: Documents listed by the programme's 'How to apply' page: (1) academic transcript including grades; (2) a personal statement / motivation letter (Apply@UniTo lists 'A motivation letter must be added to your application' under Other requirements); (3) CV; (4) any English proficiency certificate held (or the university-issued statement that the medium of instruction was English); (5) an identification document (ID/passport). Additional items required by the central UNITO/Apply@UniTo procedure for holders of a foreign qualification: the first-cycle degree certificate (or evidence of near-graduation), the official transcript of records issued by the university with signature and seal (a Diploma Supplement issued on the EC/Council of Europe/UNESCO model and containing the full transcript may be accepted as an alternative to both qualification and transcript), and proof of authenticity of the study documents where online verification is not possible - legalisation/Apostille or a Statement of Verification, with a Declaration of Value or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability/Verification requested for degree recognition. Entry-qualification documents are accepted in English, French, Italian or Spanish; if issued in any other language, both the original and a certified translation must be uploaded. Application fee: EUR 60 one-time, payable within each call's deadline, non-refundable, and unchanged whether one or two degree programmes are selected. Non-EU visa applicants must additionally complete the Universitaly pre-enrolment. uncertainty_notes:
ACCESS PROBLEMS AND METHOD: www.economics.unito.it (130.186.3.24) refused all direct HTTPS/HTTP connections from this environment (ECONNREFUSED / no response), and en.unito.it returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare). Two workarounds were used and both are official-source-based: (a) apply.unito.it was successfully retrieved in full with a browser user-agent, so all Apply@UniTo course-282 content quoted above is a DIRECT read of the live official page (retrieved 2026-09-01), including the 2026/27 deadline box, quota, entry qualification, language requirements and fees; (b) the programme microsite content was read from Internet Archive snapshots - admission_requirements.html snapshot 2025-03-01 (page's own last-update stamp 25/03/2021) and how_to_apply.html snapshot 2025-02-16 (last-update stamp 25/03/2024) - and cross-checked against 2026 search-engine renderings of the live pages, which returned the same wording. en.unito.it content was reconstructed from search-engine renderings only.

SPECIFIC UNCERTAINTIES:
1) ACADEMIC REQUIREMENTS WORDING CONFLICT. The programme microsite presents four cumulative requirements (GPA >= 90% of max AND >= 1/10 credits in Economics AND >= 1/10 credits in Math/Statistics AND English B2). Apply@UniTo instead presents the credit and B2 requirements as mandatory but the merit test as 'at least one of' (RePEc top-12.5% institution OR final grade >= 9/10). The RePEc-ranking alternative does not appear at all on the microsite. It is likely that the RePEc route is an alternative offered to holders of foreign qualifications, but this is not stated explicitly anywhere; treat the Apply@UniTo text as binding for international applicants.
2) ENGLISH CERTIFICATE - HARD REQUIREMENT OR NOT. Apply@UniTo says applicants 'must hold an international certification' at B2 (max 3 years old), with the medium-of-instruction letter as the only stated alternative. The microsite, by contrast, says that a missing English certification leads to an interview in English rather than to rejection. These two are not reconciled; the safe reading is that Apply@UniTo applicants should upload a certificate or a medium-of-instruction statement.
3) DOMESTIC APPLICATION WINDOW. The '1 March - 20 August' window for holders of an Italian degree comes from a page last updated 25/03/2024; the exact 2026 dates and the URL of the departmental application form were not verified. The microsite's own key-information sheet was seen (via search) still referencing '2024' for this window.
4) UNIVERSITALY DEADLINE. '15 July 2026' for non-EU visa applicants' pre-enrolment was read from a search-engine rendering of en.unito.it, not from a direct page read, and follows the university-wide pattern rather than a programme-specific statement.
5) '50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad' is a territorial cap on visa applicants only and does NOT make the programme restricted-access; the programme is otherwise open access. How the 50 places are allocated if oversubscribed (ranking criteria, Marco Polo sub-quota) is not published on the pages consulted.
6) FEE FIGURES are for a.y. 2025-26; Apply@UniTo explicitly directs applicants to the university portal for the a.y. 2026-27 figures, which were not published in retrievable form. UNITO has also announced that the ISEE Parificato will no longer be used to reduce tuition fees from 2026-2027, which affects international applicants' fee bracket.
7) PROGRAMME CONTACT. A search-engine rendering of the microsite gave 'master.economics@unito.it' as the programme contact address; this was not confirmed against a directly-read page.
8) NAMING AMBIGUITY. Do not confuse this LM-56 'Economics' [2304M23, Apply id 282] with the other UNITO LM-56 English-taught programmes: 'Economic Analysis and Policy' (EAP, Apply id 683, part of the EPOG-JM Erasmus Mundus consortium with its own separate EPOG application procedure and a 29 January 2026 / interviews 4-6 March 2026 calendar), 'Economics of the Environment, Culture and Territory' (Apply id 291), 'Economics of Innovation for Sustainable Development' [0404M21], and 'Economics and Finance with Data Science' (Apply id 705).
9) The 2026/27 deadline box read on apply.unito.it showed only the currently-open call (8 September 2026) because the earlier calls have already closed; the 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026 window applicable to non-EU visa applicants is taken from the university-wide 'When can I apply?' page rather than from a programme-specific statement.
